layout.identity: stable metadata id; folder path is not identity

shape.familiesNote: The array above is the executable form of this shape block: every record lives in a flat family folder directly under its feature - features/<feature>/<family>/<name>/index.yaml - with no business/, architecture/, business/srs/ or architecture/sds/ segment anywhere. This replaced an earlier generation of this schema that documented a business/{overview,srs} plus architecture/{overview,sds} nesting; the real example tree and the gate that checks it (scripts/checks/check-example-work.mjs's own FAMILIES set) never used that nesting, and this file now states the shape both of them actually use. scripts/checks/check-example-work.mjs reads shape.families from this file at gate time and refuses (FAMILIES_DRIFT) the moment its own FAMILIES set and this list disagree, so the two cannot drift apart silently a second time.
shape.br: features/<feature>/br/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/business-rule. May carry appliesTo, module (a string or list of module-root directory paths - never individual files, see the owners note under implementation below) and blockedBy.
shape.ac: features/<feature>/br/<rule>/ac/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/acceptance-criterion. Nested one level under the br it accepts rather than living in its own sibling family folder - an acceptance criterion has no identity apart from the rule it accepts. Authors rule (the owning br's id), given, when, then and carries no lifecycle state of its own (see rules, below, on which nodes author state).
shape.sds: features/<feature>/sds/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/sds-component - a logical component of the architecture map, tracing SRS paths through entry points, contracts, data, quality controls, deployment and verification. A done sds-component must carry owners: [{role, path}] naming at least one module-root directory that exists on disk (the read-scope boundary a design component describes is a module boundary, not a prose claim); a todo one without owners is warned, not refused, since the module a design targets may not exist yet.
shape.ui: features/<feature>/ui/<name>/index.yaml plus <name>/assets/**, schema work/ui-screen. Per docs/kinds.md's lane order, drawing precedes implementing: a done work/implementation that names a ui-screen in its own proves, or whose repository is the workspace's frontend repository, is refused (IMPL_BEFORE_DIRECTION) unless every relevant ui-screen - the ones it proves, or, when it proves none by id, every ui-screen its own feature owns - is itself done.
shape.impl: features/<feature>/impl/<repository>/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/implementation, one flat family folder per feature split by the repository the code lives in (<repository> is the exact value the record's own `repository` field names, e.g. impl/todo-app-backend/<name> beside impl/todo-app-frontend/<name> in a two-repository product) - never an `implementation/` singular parent with `frontend/`/`backend/` children, which no example tree or gate ever used. `owners: [{role, path}]` names one or more module-root directories, never individual files: `path` (and `work/business-rule.module`, and `work/sds-component.owners[].path` above) is the directory a reader would call the module's root - `src/modules/domain/task`, not `src/modules/domain/task/ownership.guard.ts` - so a file inside it moving during a refactor is not, by itself, a broken reference. A done implementation's every owner directory must exist on disk (OWNER_PATH_MISSING otherwise refuses it); a todo one is warned, not refused. A done implementation whose `proves` names a record that is not itself `state: done` is refused (PROVES_TARGET_NOT_DONE) - proof cannot outrun what it proves.
shape.uat: features/<feature>/uat/<name>/{index.yaml,accounts.yaml,fixtures.yaml,seed.sql,cleanup.sql, assets/,runs/<runId>/**} - see uatFlow/uatRun below for the exact shape.
shape.contract: features/<feature>/contract/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/contract - a synchronous request/response surface between a provider feature and a consumer feature; provenBy.provider/consumer each name the implementation(s) that proved their half.
shape.integration: features/<feature>/integration/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/integration - the one node a declared extensions.work3.integrations edge owes, proven only against the real external provider.
shape.gap: features/<feature>/gap/<name>/index.yaml, schema work/gap. closedBy is a list of record ids (a bare string is accepted and normalised to a one-element list, for the many gaps that only ever needed one) - a gap reaches done only once every id in closedBy is itself done, because a gap whose statement named two missing things is not honestly closed by building one of them.
shape.assets: <node>/assets/**/<file-in-original-format> - payload organization beside a record's own index.yaml, never a Work node in its own right and never given an index.yaml.
shape.runs: <uat-node>/runs/<runId>/** - append-only UAT evidence; see uatRun below for the exact file set.
shape.derived: _derived/{index.yaml,frontier.md} at the .starciwork root - GENERATED by scripts/example-derive.mjs, never authored by hand. Excluded from every record walk (it is not itself a record, has no id) and refused (scripts/checks/check-example-derived.mjs) the moment it goes stale against what is actually on disk, or the moment any real record authors a top-level usedBy/effectiveState/ frontier field of its own.
shape.uatFlow: features/<feature>/uat/<flow>/{index.yaml,accounts.yaml,fixtures.yaml,seed.sql,cleanup.sql,assets/}. The flow's index.yaml declares entry, actor, an ordered steps[] (each an action, its expected business outcome and the observed-feedback checks that apply to it), fixtures, effects and cleanup, in uat.verify's own shape. accounts.yaml keeps its work/disposable-accounts schema and stays local/synthetic, but each entry now names {role, identity} (an _resources identity id) instead of a literal password; the literal-secret shape retired with this change.
shape.uatRun: features/<feature>/uat/<flow>/runs/<runId>/{manifest.yaml,run-ledger.json,flows.json, ux-checks.json,walk.json,screens/*.png,videos/*,readback.json,cleanup.json,result.md} - the exact evidence file set uat.verify's writes.evidence names. Runs are append-only - a re-run adds a new runId, never edits a settled one. The flow's own evidence.yaml, beside its index.yaml, points at the run it settled on (a run field naming runs/<runId>). A uat-flow record reaches done only when that run has at least one file under screens/, at least one under videos/ and a result.md whose outcome is pass; until then the record stays todo and cites a gap.<feature>.live-proof record in blockedBy.
shape.designReview: Current br/fr/nfr/data/journey/decision/sds records use completion.review inside their owning index.yaml, without an evidence folder.
shape.evidence: Profiles using execution proof may retain <node>/evidence/<id>/manifest.yaml; this is not a required folder for every layer.
shape.workflowRunState: one SQLite file, .starciwork/runtime.sqlite (plus its -wal and -shm siblings), holding state, events, jobs, leases, goals, reports, contracts, checks, inbox, signals and owner inputs. Untracked. See ledger-db.md; .starciwork/_local is retired and is only an import source for ledger-migrate.
shape.workflowAnchor: .starciwork/ledger-anchor.json - TRACKED, the head of every live workflow, so a restored or rolled-back ledger is refused instead of resumed
shape.kernelCustody: .starciwork/{kernel-evidence,kernel-strays,kernel-headless,kernel-approvals}/** - kernel-owned working state with a real lifetime, untracked, excluded from Work validation, never canonical Work
shape.uiDirectionAsset: features/<feature>/ui/<screen>/assets/<name>.png with a sibling <name>.prompt.txt under the same assets/. interface.draw writes both - the record's ui block (intent, surfaces, states, coverage {scale, representativeScreens, map}, accessibility, responsive, artworkSlots, observations, gaps) and, in assets/ui.assets, one entry per representative direction with role direction and a generation object (tool image_gen.imagegen, promptPath, inputRefs) beside the prompt file's own entry with role prompt and no generation. A model name is recorded only when the tool itself exposes one; it is never authored, and it is never the host that ran the tool (an Orca-hosted run is the host, not a field). A ui record reaches done only with at least one asset carrying generation and a coverage map that names every state the record's states list names. Until interface.draw has run, the record stays todo and cites a gap.<feature>.direction-not-drawn record in blockedBy - the image is a designed op output, not something an agent types into place.
shape.frontendCaptures: features/<feature>/impl/<repository>/<name>/assets/<running-page-screenshot>, with a matching markup reference kept beside each capture. These assets never carry a generation record - that is what tells a capture and a direction apart regardless of prose provenance (see scripts/checks/render.mjs's capture-identity rule) - and a generation-bearing asset never sits outside a work/ui-screen record's own assets/.
shape.resources: .starciwork/_resources/{environments,identities,fixtures}/<name>/resource.yaml, schema work/resource (plain - see the op-vocabulary mapping below for why the op text says work/resource@1). uat.verify's reads.environment/reads.accounts/reads.fixtures and writes.resources resolve here: an environment resource names target/origins, owner, configuration revision, probes and allowedEffects; an identity resource names its provider, disposability and a custody ref into the repository's sealed secrets (never a secret value itself); a fixture resource names its schema/seed files, preconditions and run-owned namespace. A uat-flow's environment and fixtures[] fields, and its accounts.yaml's accounts[].identity field, are edges into this family and must resolve to a resource.yaml of the matching kind.

rules: SRS and SDS are the upstream source of truth for every feature and are independent of source code. SRS owns required behavior and SDS owns target technical design. UI, implementation and UAT trace to them through stable IDs; current code may prove conformance or expose a gap, but never supplies or silently redefines either root.

A business or architecture record carries two claims, and they are separate fields because they are separate facts. `state: done` says the record is agreed and implementable. `proven` - written by the kernel, naming the implementation, ui and uat nodes that demonstrated it, with the digest of the slice they demonstrated - says it has been shown to work. An empty `proven` on a done record is honest and expected: the specification is a skeleton that implementation completes. What is refused is the two collapsing into one word, because then a record that was agreed is indistinguishable from a record that was demonstrated, and the whole tree's credibility rests on telling those apart.

Implementation, ui and uat keep their own state. They are evidence of a specification AND assets with a lifetime of their own: a dependency upgrade, a security patch or a refactor is work on them while every specification stays correct. Collapsing them into pure evidence of a record would leave nowhere to schedule that work except by suspending a specification that is not wrong.

`proven` is counted, not merely stored: the ledger summary reports agreed and proven separately per kind, so the gap between a specification corpus and its demonstration is a number an owner reads rather than an inference. An unmeasured gap becomes the comfortable default.

A product's brand is one record: brand/index.yaml at the tree root, a sibling of features/, with kind brand and its masters in brand/assets/**. At most one brand node exists per tree; a second one, or a brand node anywhere else, is refused. It is a decision kind, done only through a collocated completion.review that names the rev it settled, and its brand: key is the only place colour tokens, typography, mascot, logo, iconography, imagery, voice, motion and the product-wide don'ts are authored. Every design operation reads it instead of restating it, and the record names the real frontend token or component files its machine checks compare against.

Frontend-facing nodes bind the brand implicitly: a ui node, an implementation or uat node with a frontend layout, and any node that names the brand in refs or dependsOn fold the brand's spec digest into their own inputDigest. A rev bump or a changed colour therefore suspends their completions; no authored edge per screen is required, and backend-only work is untouched.

One project owns one canonical .starciwork in its bound source repository. Its product catalog is features/index.yaml; every actual feature owns features/<feature>/{business,architecture,ui,implementation,uat}/ as applicable.

The project or repository name belongs in workspace metadata, not a wrapper directory. Do not author .starciwork/<project>/, .starciwork/business/ or .starciwork/features/business/. Individual features, FE, BE and services do not create another project workspace.

A shared rule, data definition, NFR or cross-feature journey has one accountable feature owner. Other features reference its stable ID rather than copy it or create a second product-level business tree. Parent indexes link to actual children and empty layers are not scaffolded.

Retained AI interface.draw images and real running-product screenshots both live under the bound backend .starciwork in their owning node assets/**. Identify generated design versus real capture and the actual capture environment; external/temp/chat-only media are not stored Work deliverables. Keep one owner and reference it across UI/implementation/UAT rather than copying bytes.

Each semantic scope folder has one index.yaml node and may contain further scope folders and optional assets/. The same recursive convention applies to Business, Architecture, UI, implementation/backend, implementation/frontend and UAT. Asset subfolders are payload organization, not Work nodes, and need no index.yaml. Keep small scopes flat; do not create empty template folders.
Split by independently owned questions and acceptance boundaries, not workflow stages. Names and depth stay flexible.

Canonical index.yaml uses work/node@2 metadata. New Business has a readable businessOverview and a filesystem-split SRS under functional-requirements, non-functional-requirements, business-rules, data and customer-journeys. Detailed leaves carry extensions.work3.srs with a starci/srs-* section schema. Legacy cohesive starci/specification@2 remains readable; it is not a second copy of the split SRS.

Business/index.yaml aggregates overview/index.yaml and srs/index.yaml. Each FR leaf owns its actors, trigger, main/alternative/exception flows, postconditions, refs and acceptance in the same file. NFR, rule, data, decision and journey leaves remain separate addressable owners and link through stable semantic IDs. Parent indexes aggregate; they never repeat descendant detail.
Create a detailed child only for an actual FR, NFR, rule, decision, data definition or journey. Further folders may group large scopes, but each parent still owns only aggregate metadata.

Only leaves author state: uninvestigate, todo or done. todo is confirmed incomplete work and requires no investigation receipt. done is the only state that requires bound proof. activity is auxiliary: idle, investigating, implementing or verifying. blockers[] explains impediments without becoming lifecycle state. Parents author no state or completion and derive progress from required descendants.

Authored state is a claim; effective state is the runtime's computation, and they are deliberately not the same field. A node whose bound input changed keeps `state: done` with its completion, its evidence and its history intact, and the validator derives `effectiveState: suspended` with a reason. Historical proof is never rewritten to say the work was not done - it was; what changed is the input it was proved against.

Authored `suspended` is a different word for a different thing - imported or unapproved scope, which carries a suspensionReason and never satisfies a prerequisite. The two meanings must not be merged: a re-verification of proven work and an unapproved import are opposite situations, and one word for both would schedule each as the other.

A derived state still needs a lane. A node with `effectiveState: suspended` is currently skipped by every scheduling filter, because they admit `state === 'todo'` alone - so an input-changed node keeps its proof and is never re-verified. The lane admits the derived signal, tagged as re-verification against the changed input, and the work it schedules is never re-authoring.

When investigation occurs, investigation.contextDigest binds semantic context, excluding child rollup and auxiliary activity, blockers and history. A semantic parent change makes every affected descendant effectively uninvestigate while preserving stored done, completion, history and evidence.

dependsOn uses stable node IDs; refs bind semantic inputs without implying execution order. An edge records the digest of the slice it bound, so a change invalidates exactly the dependents that bound the changed slice - one hop, at the edge. Invalidation is not transitive: a dependent whose own bound slice did not change stays as it is, and a root edit therefore cannot suspend a subtree that never read the part that moved. Where a dependent is genuinely affected it becomes suspended, keeping its proof.

Done is a current status, never an edit lock. Authorized revisions may edit the node and its owned assets. Re-evaluate changed inputs and affected dependents; never copy stale completion onto changed content. Preserve unrelated work and useful media. New required work prevents parent done; unrelated completed branches remain intact.

Freshness reports keep three conditions distinct: source drift means current implementation no longer matches an implementation completion's sourceIdentity; evidence invalidation means a canonical semantic digest or required proof changed; unavailable input means a required repository, revision, asset, tool or proof cannot be resolved. Unavailability blocks an observation without rewriting state or guessing drift. Current code never becomes SRS/SDS truth.

Impact follows declared semantic edges and the canonical digest model: ancestor specifications, child aggregation, refs, dependsOn, typed SRS/SDS links, resources and implicit frontend brand binding. A shared aggregate constraint can legitimately affect several branches; directory proximity or an unrelated SRS sibling edit cannot create a global invalidation on its own. Reports name the owner, edge and cause and never alter hash policy.
Declare semantic design/source files using node.assets with paths under own assets/. Their exact bytes contribute to semantic context; conservative hashing does not ignore presumed typo-only edits.

Record output screenshots/videos in evidence assets with scope: node and paths under the primary owner assets/. Output evidence is not also declared as a semantic input, avoiding self-invalidating proof.
Source code remains in bound repositories; code/index.yaml tracks requirements, exact source references and completion.

All structured Work records and results use YAML. JSON and underscore-prefixed directories are rejected in canonical records, except workspace-root _local for excluded execution state and workspace-root _resources for typed resource.yaml custody plus declared opaque or encrypted payloads; central schemas stay in .claude.
Repository and environment provenance is written directly in sourceRefs or the owning module record. refs and dependsOn remain stable technical node IDs for digest propagation.

UAT accounts.yaml uses schema work/disposable-accounts (the example tree's own convention; the legacy work/disposable-accounts@1 shape in work.schema.yaml embedded a literal username/password pair per entry, which is refused now that _resources/identities/** exists). Each entry is {role, identity: <_resources identity resource id>} - a sealed ref, never a synthetic password written into the flow's own tree. Images and video remain original binary assets.

Direction, capture and run are three different outputs and never share a shape. interface.draw's generated direction is a ui-owned {path, role: direction, generation: {tool: image_gen.imagegen, promptPath, inputRefs}} asset with its exact prompt kept as a sibling {role: prompt} asset; a model name is recorded only when the tool exposes one, never authored, and never the host (an Orca-run image step is the host, not a generation field). frontend.implement's implementation capture is a real running-page screenshot under implementation/frontend/assets/ with a matching markup reference and never a generation record. uat.verify's run is the append-only uat/<flow>/runs/<runId>/ evidence file set the op's writes.evidence names, settled on by the flow's sibling evidence.yaml (`run: runs/<runId>`). A generation-bearing asset outside a work/ui-screen record, or one inside a work/implementation record, is refused; a work/ui-screen or work/uat-flow record claims `done` only once its own direction asset or settled run actually exists, never by authored claim - both stay `todo` behind a `gap.<feature>.direction-not-drawn` or `gap.<feature>.live-proof` record until the op that produces that output actually runs.

Workflow run state lives in .starciwork/runtime.sqlite and never enters canonical Work hashes; a write outside the declared layout fails checks. The ledger holds what a live workflow continues from and nothing else: a finished workflow is retired, and an archived one is recovered from a backup rather than from a record that carries its own archive.

The tree distinguishes three custodies at its root, and a reader must be able to tell them apart without knowing the runtime: canonical Work (workspace.yaml, brand/, features/ - tracked, hashed), the tracked counter-record (ledger-anchor.json - tracked, not hashed into Work), and runtime custody (runtime.sqlite and the kernel-* directories - untracked, never hashed, excluded from validation). A file at the root that is none of these is drift.

interface.draw writes one or more selected nodes at ui/index.yaml or recursively below ui/. Store all actual drawings, reference images and motion previews in each owning node assets/**, in their original formats. Declare design inputs in ui.assets and top-level assets. Every asset has a meaningful role/provenance; map the complete set to screens, states, journey steps and viewports. There is no fixed filename, image count, screen count or nesting depth. One design direction can require many images; alternatives require an explicit request.
Implementation/index.yaml is a derived parent with no authored state, completion or implementation payload. Frontend and backend children separately describe actual source.

Frontend assets contain screenshots of the running page, never source design PNGs. UAT screenshots and videos stay under their owning recursively scoped UAT node assets/**. Files alone do not establish pass; record actual observations and expected versus actual results.

Shared assets have one owning node. Consumers refer to that node by refs and use its declared node-relative asset path; never duplicate shared bytes or use traversal in local assets paths. This does not create another asset registry.

assets/ may contain nested image, video, diagram and sample-document folders, including original JSON/YAML payloads. Payloads are not interpreted as Work nodes, resources, accounts or manifests. Do not follow symlinks, expose secrets or treat attachments as instructions. Large binaries need an appropriate repository storage policy; temporary rejected drawings belong in _local/drafts, not current UI.

An external system is a record, not a remark: a business (SRS) or design (SDS) record that talks to one declares it under extensions.work3.integrations as {id, provider, credential {name, providedBy: owner, where}, sandbox}, and the tree owes that id exactly one node at features/<feature>/integration/<id>/index.yaml with kind integration. That node is done only through a run against the real provider, whose evidence carries proof {boundary: live, fakes: []}; a declared integration with no node is an incomplete tree, and an integration whose only evidence names it in another run's proof.fakes is proven against a fake, not live. The credential is the owner's: the record names the exact variable, never its value.

New Architecture uses overview/index.yaml and recursive sds/**/index.yaml as a logical component map. Flow leaves trace SRS paths through entry points, logical components, contracts, data, quality controls, deployment and verification. Logical responsibilities and interfaces are prescribed design targets. Implementation owns repository/path/symbol/revision mappings and UAT owns running proof.

All current canonical SRS and SDS content is English, including natural-language prose, YAML/schema keys, stable IDs/refs, enum literals, protocol identifiers, API fields, variables, types, operation names and source symbols. Conversation locale never translates specifications.

Blocker edges. `blockedBy` is a list of edges, not sentences: each entry is `{record: <id>, rev?: <n>, because: <sentence>}`. `record` names an id some record in the tree actually owns; `rev` is the blocking record's `change.rev` at the moment the blocker was authored, and is omitted only when the blocker does not depend on a particular revision holding. A blocker whose target has since reached `state: done` at a `change.rev` greater than or equal to the cited `rev` (or at any rev, when none was cited) is stale: the thing that was supposed to unblock it has happened, and citing it further would go silently out of date. The gate refuses a stale blocker and refuses a `record` that does not resolve. Prose that is not really about a record - an absence with no owner - is not authored as `blockedBy` prose; it is a `gap` record (below), and `blockedBy` points at its id like any other.

Blockers form a DAG, and a cycle in it is refused outright (BLOCKER_CYCLE): nothing can honestly wait on something that is itself waiting on it, so a `blockedBy` chain that reaches back to a record already on its own walk is a structural impossibility, not a fact about the work. A chain's real root - the reason nothing further needs authoring - is a `work/gap` or an open `work/policy-decision` (`outcome: open`); a chain that dead-ends at an ordinary record instead (neither cyclic nor gap/open- decision rooted) is warned rather than refused (BLOCKER_UNROOTED), because forcing a gap to be authored for every such dead end in one pass would be a larger sweep than any single change should make - the warning names the actual unrooted target so the fact stays visible until a gap is written for it.

Known absences are records, not restated prose. `work/gap` lives at `features/<feature>/gap/<name>/index.yaml`, id `gap.<feature>.<name>`, and carries `state: todo|done` and a plain `statement` of the fact that is missing - an event nobody emits yet, a field no data record declares, a module that has not been written under the stack the project is moving to. An optional `closedBy: <record id>` names the record whose completion actually closes the gap, so a reader can tell an open absence from one already scheduled to close. `blockedBy` and `conflictsWith` point at a gap's id exactly as they would at any other record, so the same absence is named once and every dependent points at that one name instead of restating it.

Pairwise conflicts, and the sibling for sets. `conflictsWith` stays a list of `{record: <id>, rev?: <n>, because: <sentence>}` for two records that currently cannot both be true. The gate resolves `record` and, when `rev` is cited, refuses a mismatch against the target's current `change.rev`. Three or more records that are each individually true and jointly unsatisfiable are not a chain of pairwise conflicts; they are a set only the settling decision can resolve, so `tension: {records: [<id>, <id>, ...], statement: <sentence>}` is authored on the `work/policy-decision` record that owns settling them, and refused anywhere else. The gate requires every id in `records` to resolve and at least two of them.

A decision's vocabulary is closed. `work/policy-decision` authors `outcome: open | decided`, `options: [{id, consequence, summary?}]`, `chosen?: <option id>` (required exactly when `outcome: decided`, and refused unless it names an id present in `options`), and an optional `blocks: [<record id>]` naming what the decision's settling unblocks. A decision does not invent its own outcome vocabulary by writing the chosen option's id (or any other free-form word) directly into `outcome`, and it does not carry a `targetModule` or similar ad hoc pointer to where the decision will eventually be implemented - that belongs to the `implementation` record that later proves it, not the decision.

Change is authored, staleness is derived, and neither is folklore. `change: {rev, kind: initial|editorial|clarifying|breaking, at, withdraws?: [<exact statement>], retains?: [<exact statement>], reason?}` records one authored edit; `withdraws` names statements this rev removes verbatim and `retains` names statements an editorial pass keeps verbatim, so a change that removes half a sentence is not forced to withdraw the whole thing to be honest about what moved. On `work/evidence`, `stale?: true`, `staleSince?: {record: <id>, rev?: <n>}` and `staleReason?` say a passed run no longer speaks for the record beside it. The digest that decides this is the kernel's own: sha256 of the record's `index.yaml` file bytes, exactly as `kernel/reconciliation.mjs`'s `recordDigests`/`nodeFileOf` compute it for reconciliation. An `evidence.yaml` whose `recordDigest` does not equal that digest, computed now, must carry `stale: true`; the gate refuses one that does not. Staleness is never cleared by editing `recordDigest` to match - only a fresh run, which is a kernel act, retires it.

`work/evidence`'s `provenance.actor` names who ran the assertions, and the value is a claim that must be true, not a label of convenience. `starci-kernel` means a live kernel workflow's own `ctx.work.api.markDone` write settled the record, re-running the checks itself. `example-evidence` means `scripts/example-evidence.mjs` produced the file by actually running the given commands outside any kernel workflow, against one of the example trees - a real run, with a real recordDigest, just not one a kernel operation performed. Neither actor authors `state` on the record beside it; only a person or a kernel operation does that.

Done means proven or says so. A record with `state: done` needs a sibling `evidence.yaml`, or an authored `verificationSource: authored-claim` with a `because:` sentence saying why no run proves it. `work/data`, `work/brand` and `work/policy-decision` are authored claims by nature - a data shape, a brand token or a settled decision is true because it was written down and agreed, not because a test ran - so the gate treats every `done` record of those three schemas as satisfying this rule without the declaration being repeated on each one. Every other schema needs the evidence file or the explicit declaration; the gate refuses a `done` record of any other schema that has neither.

A rule may constrain a record it does not own. `work/business-rule` and `work/sds-component` may carry `appliesTo: [<record id>]`, an outbound edge naming a record - owned by any feature - that the rule's or component's requirement reaches even though the rule does not own it and does not edit it. The gate only resolves the ids; it does not require the target to acknowledge the edge back. The derived consequence is one sentence: a `done` record that acquires an `appliesTo` edge newer than its proof reads as `effectiveState: suspended` until it is re-proven against the new constraint, the same way a changed input suspends a record that read it. `appliesTo` is refused on any other schema - `work/data` in particular does not carry it, because a data record's relationship to the rules it embodies is `refs`, an inbound reading, not an outbound constraint on a record it does not own.

Events are a family; data may extend data; time may trigger. `work/event` lives at `features/<feature>/event/<name>/index.yaml`, id `event.<feature>.<name>`, and authors `producer: <record id>` (the record whose flow raises it), `payload: [{name, type, note?}]` and `delivery: {guarantee: at-least-once|at-most-once|exactly-once, ordering: none|per-key|total}`. A consumer declares `subscribes: [<event id>]`, each id resolving to a `work/event` record; `work/contract` remains for a synchronous request/response surface and is not overloaded to describe a fire-and-forget signal. On `work/data`, `extends?: <data id>` names a base data record this one specializes, with `adds: [<field definition>, ...]` listing only the fields the base does not already declare - the shared fields are inherited, not repeated as a fresh disagreement about the base's shape. On `stateMachine.transitions[]`, `on` may be the plain string it always was, or `{timer: <duration or plain-language description>}` when what actually fires the transition is a clock, not an event - a digest window closing, a scheduled tick - and the gate accepts either shape.

Implementation names owners, plural. `work/implementation` authors `owners: [{role, path}]` - each entry the path of one real or intended artifact and the role it plays (`module`, `route`, `entry`, `block`, or another short word naming the kind of unit) - because one screen or one flow can span more than one owned artifact (a route adapter, a feature entry, a connected block and its pure twin) and a single `directory`/`files` pair cannot name more than one shape at a time. `work/business-rule.module` may be a plain string, for the ordinary one-module case, or a list of strings when the rule's module genuinely spans more than one path. The gate refuses `directory`/`files` on `work/implementation`; that shape is retired in favor of `owners`, and the gate refuses an `owners` entry missing either `role` or `path`.

Two topologies host the same record tree. In a multi-repository product, `.starciwork` lives in the bound backend repository and `.workspaces/projects/<project>/{be,fe}.json` at the host routes each side to its repository and its `architecture.json` roots (`examples/todo-app-backend` paired with `examples/todo-app-frontend` demonstrates this shape). In a monorepo, `.starciwork` lives at the repository root and `architecture.json` names `apps/*`/`packages/*` as its roots instead of a second repository. Both host the identical `features/<feature>/{business,architecture,ui,implementation,uat}` tree; only where `.starciwork` sits and how its roots are declared differ, and a project does not run both shapes for the same product at once.

content.en: Every authored index.yaml is a work/node@2 record at its catalog-declared path under features/<feature>/architecture/. Author overview plus typed extensions.work3.sds leaves in flows, components, contracts, data, quality, deployment, decisions and verification - each leaf payload carrying its declared starci/sds-*@1 section const. Parent indexes carry only starci/sds-aggregate@1 metadata. Components prescribe logical responsibilities and interfaces without repository roles, paths, symbols, signatures, source status or revision evidence. Write all canonical SDS content in English, including natural-language prose, YAML/schema keys, stable IDs/refs, enum literals, protocol identifiers, API fields, variables, types, operation names and source symbols. Preserve Business and shared design through stable IDs and exact owning Work refs.

Only for a selected job matrix, return the exact request-bound result. Populate every declared cell output with actual canonical Work/source/runtime references or produced JSON artifacts from this job; retain real artifact bytes and hashes. Do not rename/regenerate upstream expectations. Missing required output/evidence remains blocked or failed and cannot advance. The selected request freezes output field schemas before execution.

action.en: Resolve accepted SRS scope, drivers, actors and platform constraints from canonical Work. Read specifications/sds-map.json and docs/architecture-sds.md. Survey relevant source, configuration and installed APIs; then independently record retain, extend, correct, replace or add decisions with rationale, impact and migration. Prescribe logical responsibilities, interfaces, state and failure behavior. Repository/file/symbol/call mappings and actual revisions or proof belong to Implementation. Never write product code or present a design constraint as deployed behavior.

Write logical components with responsibilities, exclusions and dependency directions. Contracts have one owner, caller/receiver, sync/async/in-process mode, inputs, outcomes/errors, authority, timeout, retry, idempotency and compatibility. Import shared views by stable Work/item IDs; never copy or redefine another owner contract. A generic inter-module command requires an advertised recipient capability, versioned payload, valid installations, authority and consent, stable intent plus fingerprint, and recipient-owned effect/receipt. Admission is not delivery or business completion; an unknown response reconciles the same intent. Never create an arbitrary-payload effect endpoint.

Design runtime scenarios referencing canonical SRS flow IDs. Every step names its component, target repo/path/symbol/signature, callers/callees, contracts, authorization, data, transaction/state decision, return path, failure outcome, recovery and planned verification. Do not attach source status or revision evidence. Cover significant architectural differences, including response loss, concurrency, duplicates, ordering, partial success and cancellation where relevant.

Specify authoritative versus rebuildable data, storage, isolation, consistency, lifecycle, placement, connections and credential custody. For durable customer state, examine database consistency, complete backup set, authoritative/derived state, volumes, config, Secrets/keys, custody outside the relevant failure domain, restore destination/order, reconciliation, old-writer fencing and safe effect resumption. Volume bytes alone do not prove recovery. Select failure domains and recovery depth from actual scope, not a mandatory checklist for every project.

Challenge one coherent proposal with a materially simpler alternative, rationale, cost, downsides and revisit conditions. Patterns are optional; specify actual mechanisms rather than names. Use applicable StarCi knowledge, verified installed APIs and primary technical references with an applicability argument. Do not invent business targets or product policy; make technical choices within approved requirements.

Write relevant quality/threat/failure scenarios with trigger, impact, response, owner and planned design checks linked to SRS acceptance. Keep residual risk and limitations explicit. Never claim source implementation, security audit, HA verification or a recovery drill ran from a design document.

Validate recursive layout and exact canonical SRS/shared-design references. Review full requirement/flow/acceptance coverage across the owning architecture scope. Resolve material design blockers before pass. Confirm that all canonical SDS content is English; schema validity alone is not review. Implementation owns source mapping and test execution. Done means current reviewed design, never an edit lock.

Repair mode (the `architecture.revise` kind this operator also carries) is not a second decision: a design section a builder found silent, confusing or self-contradictory is revised here, never escalated and never left for the build to invent a mechanism around. Read the reported gap, state the two or three readings the recorded design actually admits, and choose the most reasonable one from the accepted requirement it realises, the rest of the design it must stay consistent with, the decided records of the other features and the product's own conventions. Write that reading into the section with the contract and the acceptance an implementer derives code from, bump the record's rev, and append EXACTLY ONE extensions.work3.decisionLog entry {rev, at, gap, chosen, why, alternatives}, never rewriting or deleting an earlier one. One exception: when the readings differ in an observable outcome about money, authority or customer data, do not choose silently - report ask with question.kind decision, one numbered option per reading with what each costs and who it affects, and one recommendation; the kernel writes that decision record for the owner and carries the work on the recommendation until they answer. Never ask for anything else. A gap that is really a missing or self-contradictory REQUIREMENT is blocked with srs-gap back to the business record that owns it.

requirement.en: Run the record-class validator `starci validate`; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done. Legacy specification@3 remains a readable compatibility input, never new authoring output.

Each significant operation resolves logical owner, contract, data/commit boundary, authorization, state/transaction, return/recovery and planned verification for the selected implementation slice. The Implementation handoff names the required source-mapping scope without putting repository paths or symbols into SDS. Proactively walk realistic main, alternative, failure and edge cases and relevant constraints; foreseeable material cases and core choices must not be left for implementers to invent. Explicit unknowns and subsequent empirical refinement do not require theoretical perfection before coding.

SRS outcomes map to owned contracts, runtime scenarios and design checks. Assess relevant threats/failures and limitations. Structural validation does not establish semantic approval or executed behavior.

Every revision of an already-decided record leaves three things together or it is a defect: the record changed, its rev higher than it was, and exactly one new extensions.work3.decisionLog entry naming the gap, the chosen reading, why it is the most reasonable one by the records it was read from, and the alternatives that were not taken. A changed record with no entry is a defect. A reading that changes an observable outcome about money, authority or customer data and was taken without a decision record with numbered options and one recommendation is a defect, whatever else the revision gets right.

action.en: Bind the exact operation/AC set and inspect existing code plus sibling conventions, including DI/module registration and every relevant caller. Reuse already conforming behavior. Own preparation through delivery: inspect readiness and reproduce the requested defect when applicable, partition the selected work into cohesive changes and check callers before editing. Resolve repository-local dependencies and bounded development runtime needs under the existing scope. Shared library changes belong to the actual FE or BE package owner: include owner tests, packaging/export compatibility and selected consumer integration proof in this same implementation; never publish a package implicitly. Keep shared paths exclusive and report a missing required external authority rather than inventing a helper. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers. CALL POINT (discovery, implementation or verification): when an observed source/test fact proves the accepted SDS technically missing or contradictory while business and SRS stay unchanged, read backend.implement/secondary.json and request its implementation.architecture role. The backend worker waits and never edits SDS. Orca runs architecture.decide in a separate child worktree; after coordinator review/integration, start a fresh backend attempt from that SDS revision and rerun every affected check. Implement transport, validation, permission checks, use-case logic and persistence inside the declared ownership. Enforce denials before unauthorized side effects; do not invent fallback behavior.
Implement declared transaction, retry/idempotency, concurrency, error identity and read-time revalidation. Migrations are source only; applying them remotely is not included.

Add or repair scoped unit tests, then execute the repository's backend unit gate and retain command, exit code, counts and sanitized output. Positive, denial, invalid-input and applicable race/reload cases must map to the selected operations. Unit success cannot substitute for E2E, and an unavailable runner, dependency, environment or required case is blocked/not-run rather than pass. Preserve failures, repair only within the approved goal, rerun affected gates, and never delegate this responsibility to frontend or UAT.

Review the diff and verify no unrelated changes. Commit only when authorized, then read back the full SHA/diff and prove the tested tree corresponds to that commit; otherwise report uncommitted or no-change honestly. A frontend support response must return codeRefs, changedPaths, apiContract, runtime, qualityEvidence and testedCommit bound to the caller request. Missing or not-run unit/E2E proof, commit mismatch, or unavailable required served runtime blocks the handoff, so frontend cannot consume it as verified backend. sideEffects: generated placeholder mascot/logo asset bytes under the brand record's own assets

purpose.en: Read the existing selected brand record, its ancestor scope, declared refs/dependencies/assertions, its current `rev` and validator freshness. There is exactly one brand record per product: this op revises that record rather than adding a second identity. An absent target is a scope/graph gap: report it and propose a separately selected scope op; never create a second brand owner here.

reads.path: .starciwork/<business>/business/**/index.yaml + the selected request and the owner's recorded rulings

purpose.en: Read the accepted business scope and the owner's actual rulings about identity - the name, the primary hue, whether danger may match primary, the mascot and what it may never appear in, the voice. A taste decision belongs to the owner: an unanswered one is a question with the closed options, never a choice this op makes on the owner's behalf. Inferring identity from a competitor, a template or a screenshot is not a ruling.

reads.path: consuming app manifest/lockfile + resolved component package exports/types/renderers/CSS + app family root/style imports

purpose.en: Resolve the installed design grammar from the actual consuming app, honoring workspace aliases and bundler resolution, and record package identity, version, resolved path and inspected file hashes. The family's own token names are the vocabulary this record may use: a colour is declared as the grammar token the renderer actually consumes, never as a free-floating hex value with an invented name. A similarly named family variable is not proof it is wired.

Read the real token and style files of the frontend repository - the app's global CSS, the family root, the theme and token files the owner named or that this repository actually contains - and record each file path with the exact declaration every token value comes from. These files are the source of truth for a value: this op copies them, it never proposes a palette the product does not already serve. A source file the record names and that does not exist is an environment blocker, never a value filled in from memory.

Read the mascot, logo and icon-set assets that already exist - beside the record and in the frontend repository - with their formats, dimensions and provenance. Reuse an existing verified asset before producing any new one; an asset whose rights or origin are unknown is reported, not adopted.

reads.path: knowledge/INDEX.json + applicable UI presentation/composition and installed family topics

purpose.en: Read the applicable presentation, composition and family topics before mapping a decision onto a token name, a contrast floor or an icon rule. Knowledge explains ownership and composition; the installed package and the real source files determine what a value may actually be.

reads.path: model/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Resolve this operator's request-bound external-agent chain from the selected StarCi skill and active profiles, and establish whether an image generator is actually available to this runtime. Use current host model configuration; historical model names are not availability proof. Capabilities are the intersection of actual tools, selected profile policy, op permissions and existing task authority.

content.en: Write the whole identity into the one brand record (schema work/node@2): identity (name and the installed grammar family), colour tokens as grammar token name -> value with role and the policy that governs them (`dangerMayMatchPrimary`, `minContrast`), typography, mascot, logo, iconography, imagery, voice, motion, the explicit forbidden list, the `artworkSlots` conventions every later prompt fills, and `sources` naming the real files each value was read from. Every asset path recorded under `brand.mascot`/`brand.logo` is also declared in top-level assets for byte binding. Bump `rev` once per accepted revision and state what changed. No product code, no second brand owner and no identity claim the owner did not rule.

Store reused or newly generated identity bytes under the brand record's own assets in their actual formats, each with its sha256 and its provenance. A mascot the product does not yet have may be produced once as an explicit placeholder from the owner's description with the available image generator; it is recorded as a placeholder, never as the final mascot and never as a capture of a shipped surface. When no generator is actually available, record a concrete deferred brief instead and leave the slot empty: a missing file is never described as generated.

Retain the actual output of the brand checks with their exit status, the token-to-source trace (token name, value, file and declaration it was read from), the resolved package/family evidence and the provenance of every asset. An honest not-run or failing check cannot earn done.

action.en: Freeze the brief before writing anything: the product name, the actually installed grammar family, and each identity decision the owner has ruled - primary hue, whether danger may match primary, the mascot and where it may never appear, typography, voice. Record the decisions as closed options with the ruling that selected them; an unruled taste decision is a question with the options, never a preference this op supplies. Resolve the execution profile and whether an image generator is actually available before planning any asset work; this selects no model and spawns no worker.

Derive every colour token from the real source files and nothing else: open the app's global CSS, family root and theme/token files, and for each value record the token name the renderer consumes, the value, and the exact file and declaration it came from. Map the owner's decisions onto those grammar token names rather than inventing a parallel palette. A value you cannot trace to a declaration in a real file is not written: it is a question naming the token and the file it should live in. Declare `sources` as that exact file list.

Give every token its role (primary, danger and the rest) and write the policy that governs the set - whether danger may match primary, and the minimum contrast every text-on-surface pair must hold. Check the pairs the record itself declares against that floor and against the policy, and record the measured ratios. A token set that cannot satisfy the owner's ruling and the floor at the same time is reported with both numbers, never quietly adjusted to pass.

Settle the mascot, the logo and the icon set. Reuse the assets the repository already has, with their real paths and provenance. Only when the product has no mascot asset at all, generate one explicit placeholder from the owner's description with the available image generator, store it under the record's own assets with its sha256, and record it as a placeholder pending the owner's acceptance; if the runtime has no generator, write a concrete deferred brief instead and never claim a file exists. Write `allowedIn`, `forbiddenIn` and the usage rules for each, and name the single icon set the product may use so no later screen introduces a second one.

Write the rules that make every later surface derive from this record rather than from taste: imagery style with its explicit forbidden list and `promptRules` that require every later image prompt to state this brand by name, family, palette and mascot policy; the `artworkSlots` conventions a drawing fills; voice; motion; and one forbidden list the record is judged against. A rule nobody could check from the record is rewritten until it can be.

Run the brand checks against the real frontend repository and keep their output: token values match their declared sources, every declared text pair holds the contrast floor, primary and danger are distinct unless the policy permits otherwise, every declared mascot asset exists with its recorded hash, and the icon set is the only one named. Bump `rev` and record what changed. Report `done` exactly once with the new `rev`, the checks and the token-to-source trace; a failing check is `failed` with its output; a value that cannot be traced to a source is `ask` naming the token and the file; a source file the record needs and that does not exist is `blocked` with `environment` and the exact path. Never report done on unrun checks.

requirement.en: Run the record-class validator `starci validate`; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done.

Every colour token in the record names the grammar token the renderer consumes and the exact source file and declaration its value was read from, and `sources` lists those files. A value with no traceable source is a question, never a record entry; a resolved package name and version alone is not a trace.

The machine checks ran against the actual frontend repository and their real output is retained with its exit status: source match, contrast floor, primary/danger distinctness under the declared policy, mascot assets present with their recorded hashes, and a single icon set. A green summary without retained output is not proof.

Every identity asset the record declares exists under the record's own assets with its sha256 and its provenance, and a generated placeholder is recorded as a placeholder. A deferred asset carries a concrete brief and an empty slot; no missing file is described as generated or accepted.

condition.en: A token/style source file this record must read does not exist in the selected repository, or the repository itself is not resolvable. Report `blocked` with `environment` and the exact path; never substitute a remembered value for an unreadable file.

A required token value cannot be traced to a declaration in a real source file, or two sources disagree about it. Report `ask` naming the token, the candidate values and the files; never write the value you would have chosen.

An identity decision the record needs - primary hue, whether danger may match primary, the mascot and its forbidden placements - has no owner ruling, or the ruling contradicts the contrast floor. Report `ask` with the closed options and what each one costs.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

Not for product code changes; not to invent palette/typography the bound source does not serve.

Applicable UI knowledge topics; environment/identity resources.

Downstream authority consumed by interface.draw candidates and interface.asset slot generation.

When source exists/is selected, resolve repository resource, actual checkout/root/HEAD and dirty state; read applicable instructions, manifests, owning code, callers and relevant tests. purpose.en: Classify each statement as intent, observed fact, example, proposal, unknown or contradiction, with source citation/revision. Existing behavior does not authorize a new rule.
Read the JSON field contract and this operator procedure before authoring the .starciwork payload.

Only when explicitly selected in a job matrix, read the exact cell ID, operation, immutable input bindings, requested output JSON shapes and required criteria. Standalone execution needs no fabricated matrix request. A template is not authority for extra effects.

Use current host model configuration; historical model names are not availability proof. content.en: Every authored index.yaml is a work/node@2 record at its catalog-declared path under features/<feature>/business/. Author business/overview/index.yaml with businessOverview for readable purpose, customer understanding, outcome, scope and open questions. Author typed extensions.work3.srs leaves under functional-requirements, non-functional-requirements, business-rules, policy-decisions, data and customer-journeys - each leaf payload carrying its declared starci/srs-*@1 section const. Every item owns a folder/index.yaml; every intermediate index carries only starci/srs-aggregate@1 metadata. Keep each FR's main, alternative and exception flows, branch review, postconditions and acceptance together. Write all canonical SRS content in English, including natural-language prose, YAML/schema keys, stable IDs/refs, enum literals, protocol identifiers, API fields, variables, types, operation names and source symbols. Stable semantic refs resolve through exact owning Work refs without copying.

Record current requirement-to-acceptance review on the owning node after contradictions and blockers are resolved. This is not implementation evidence and never carries a prior done or rewritten digest across changed content.

Only for a selected job matrix, return the exact request-bound result. Populate every declared cell output with actual canonical Work/source/runtime references or produced JSON artifacts from this job; retain real artifact bytes and hashes. Do not rename/regenerate upstream expectations. Missing required output/evidence remains blocked or failed and cannot advance. The selected request freezes output field schemas before execution.

action.en: Resolve the canonical .starciwork workspace and selected business leaf. Research accepted intent and supplied domain documents. Classify every citation as accepted intent, observed source, proposal or unknown; source behavior never approves policy. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Write purpose, scope/exclusions, glossary, assumptions, actors with responsibilities/rights/restrictions, FR/BR and observable NFRs. Specify business data attributes, validation, sensitivity, states/transitions and external inputs/outputs/errors. State why a data or external-interface inventory is empty. Source observations and supplied technical constraints are not approved business policy; unknown numeric targets retain a decision owner.

Every FR resolves to a detailed flow, not a title alone: trigger, primary/supporting actors, inputs, preconditions, numbered actor/request/system-response steps, guards, effects, failures, repeat behavior and success/failure postconditions. Alternative and exception branches identify their starting step, condition, ordered steps, resume/end and acceptance. Review denied/invalid input, cancellation, duplicate/retry, concurrency and recovery where relevant; explain absent branch classes without fabricating cases.

Review observable outcomes against accepted intent and observed behavior. Business states what users and the system must do, not class inheritance, repositories, service placement, Saga/CQRS, Kubernetes or backup tooling. Preserve genuinely supplied technical constraints as sourced external constraints; hand implementation questions to Architecture instead of encoding an invented design in requirements.

Specify actor-action-resource permissions, tenant/owner boundaries, sensitive-data handling and abuse cases. Give each security requirement an observable denial/no-side-effect acceptance scenario; do not mistake a disabled UI control for server enforcement.

Author business/overview/index.yaml for readable intent and typed extensions.work3.srs leaves under functional-requirements, non-functional-requirements, business-rules, policy-decisions, data and customer-journeys. Every item owns a folder/index.yaml; intermediate indexes carry only starci/srs-aggregate@1 metadata. Keep each FR's flows, branch review, postconditions and acceptance cohesive. Write all canonical SRS content in English, including natural-language prose, YAML/schema keys, stable IDs/refs, enum literals, protocol identifiers, API fields, variables, types, operation names and source symbols. Connect semantic IDs to exact owning Work refs.

Repair mode (the `business.revise` kind this operator also carries) is not a second decision: a requirement that is silent, ambiguous or settled twice in two ways is revised here, never escalated and never left for a builder to read a meaning into. Read the reported gap, state the two or three readings the recorded requirement actually admits, and choose the most reasonable one from the accepted records of this feature, the decided records of the other features and the product's own conventions. Write that reading into the requirement, rule or journey with the acceptance an implementer derives code from, bump the record's rev, and append EXACTLY ONE extensions.work3.decisionLog entry {rev, at, gap, chosen, why, alternatives}, never rewriting or deleting an earlier one. One exception: when the readings differ in an observable outcome about money, authority or customer data, do not choose silently - report ask with question.kind decision, one numbered option per reading with what each costs and who it affects, and one recommendation; the kernel writes that decision record for the owner and carries the work on the recommendation until they answer. Never ask for anything else.

Validate detailed requirement/flow/branch/acceptance coverage and the recursive Work graph. Review contradictions, scope and unresolved decisions with the user. A complete branch rolls up only from valid required leaves; draft placeholders and schema validity cannot earn done. Output reviewed business outcomes and observable security/quality acceptance for Architecture; no implementation or deployed-proof claim. Return the selected matrix's request-bound typed outputs when applicable.

requirement.en: Run the record-class validator `starci validate`; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done.
Each applicable FR/NFR/BR has acceptance IDs and source intent; no vague fast/secure/user-friendly NFR is accepted as measurable. Implementation/UAT status is untouched.

Every FR has a detailed actor flow and acceptance, every alternative/exception has ordered steps and postconditions, and security has observable negative acceptance. Validate nested ownership and every split SRS section contract; no code/service inventory is required in Business. Legacy specification@2 and srs@3 are compatibility inputs, never new output.

Every revision of an already-decided record leaves three things together or it is a defect: the record changed, its rev higher than it was, and exactly one new extensions.work3.decisionLog entry naming the gap, the chosen reading, why it is the most reasonable one by the records it was read from, and the alternatives that were not taken. A changed record with no entry is a defect. A reading that changes an observable outcome about money, authority or customer data and was taken without a decision record with numbered options and one recommendation is a defect, whatever else the revision gets right.

condition.en: A required rule, actor permission, numeric target or acceptance result has no authoritative decision.

Accepted sources conflict on an observable outcome about money, authority or customer data; preserve both citations and put the numbered options with one recommendation to the actual owner, never average them. A conflict that changes no such outcome is not this blocker - it is revised to the most reasonable reading with the reason in the decision log.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

operators.goal: Restructure one selected slice of code under a proven behavior invariant - the same regression check run before and after the change - never a behavior edit disguised as a refactor.

goal.en: Restructure one selected slice of code under a proven behavior invariant - the same regression check run before and after the change - never a behavior edit disguised as a refactor.

sideEffects: owned source edits that restructure without changing observable behavior
scoped local commits when authorized
the declared regression and architecture checks run before and after in their declared sandbox

graphPolicy.location: .starciwork node dependsOn/refs with direct sourceRefs and collocated assets

purpose.en: Read the existing selected N/index.yaml, ancestor scope, declared refs/dependencies/assertions and validator freshness. This consumer op requires its target node to exist. An absent target is a scope/graph gap: report it and propose a separately selected scope op; do not create a target or invent its acceptance/graph here.

Read accepted requirements, decisions, constraints and acceptance IDs declared as relevant inputs in the selected .starciwork graph. Intent governs the behavior that must be preserved; a needed missing input is a reported graph/scope gap, not a silently added dependency.

Read the declared boundaries, contracts, data ownership and rationale the restructure must stay inside. A refactor that needs a different contract or boundary is a design change, not a refactor - report the gap instead of stretching this op.

Resolve repository resource, actual checkout/root/HEAD and dirty state; read applicable instructions, manifests, the owning code, every caller and the existing tests. The restructure binds the exact inspected tree; a proposed change to a file that was not opened is not a refactor plan.

reads.path: repository:<repo-id>/<manifest-paths> + the slice's existing regression suite and its real runner

purpose.en: Establish before any edit which declared check actually exercises the slice's observable behavior and that it can run in this environment. The check must exist, cover the changed surface and run verbatim - a test suite that does not exist, does not cover the slice or cannot run is reported `blocked` with blocker kind `test-gap`, which routes to test.author; it is never a reason to skip the invariant or to write the missing coverage inside this op.

Read the adopted naming, error-identity, structure and typing conventions the restructure must preserve or improve toward - a refactor that degrades declared pattern conformance is a regression, not a cleanup. Load the applicable FE or BE topic files for the selected repository only; conventions never authorize behavior changes.

When the slice lives in a checked FE/BE repository, read the sealed architecture and code-pattern machines' supported arguments, report schema, exit codes and coverage limits. The same machine set runs verbatim BEFORE and AFTER the restructure; an architecture or pattern regression introduced by a pure refactor is a failure, not a refactor outcome. This read grants no fix-flag or repair authority.

Only when explicitly selected in a job matrix, read the exact cell ID, operation, immutable input bindings, requested output JSON shapes and required criteria. Standalone execution needs no fabricated matrix request. A template is not authority for extra effects.

reads.path: model/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Resolve this operator's request-bound external-agent chain from the selected StarCi skill and active profiles. Use current host model configuration; historical model names are not availability proof. Capabilities are the intersection of actual tools, selected profile policy, op permissions and existing task authority. Do not revive V2 dispatch chains, retired profiles or extra-agent permissions.

content.en: Read the existing selected scope, expected assertions and .starciwork graph unchanged. Write only state/blocker/completion here; actual observations, findings, commit mappings and remaining cleanup belong to the evidence result, not semantic node prose. Missing refs/dependencies/acceptance require a reported gap or separately selected scope update; never add/remove them to obtain pass.

Only exact owned paths in the approved code-scope, restructured without observable behavior change - moves, renames, extractions, deletions of dead code and equivalent rewrites. No feature, fix, contract, schema or configuration change rides inside a refactor; a needed behavior change is a separate selected operation, never an edit hidden in this one.

writes.path: E/manifest.yaml + E/regression-before.json + E/regression-after.json + E/architecture-before.json + E/architecture-after.json + E/diff-map.json + E/result.md

content.en: Store the exact regression command, cwd/repo, source commit/tree, exit code, counts and sanitized output for the before run and for the after run - the same command on both sides of the change. Store the same machine-check reports before and after where the slice lives in a checked repository. Map every moved or renamed symbol to its destination and record the full diff summary. Operator-specific observed result in E/result.md: the before/after parity statement with the observed outputs, and any behavior difference found - which is a failure, not a refactor outcome.

Only for a selected job matrix, return the exact request-bound result. Populate every declared cell output with actual canonical Work/source/runtime references or produced JSON artifacts from this job; retain real artifact bytes and hashes. Do not rename/regenerate upstream expectations. Missing required output/evidence remains blocked or failed and cannot advance. The selected request freezes output field schemas before execution.

action.en: Bind the exact restructure request and inspect the slice plus every caller. Select the one declared regression check that exercises the slice's observable behavior and run it BEFORE the first edit, verbatim, keeping command, tree/commit, exit code, counts and sanitized output. Where the slice lives in a checked FE/BE repository, run starci code-patterns check --profile <nest|next> --root ROOT --all BEFORE the first edit too and keep the machine report and exit code. A green baseline is the invariant's left side; a red baseline is reported failed with the observed output - a refactor does not begin on a suite already red. No existing, covering, runnable check is reported `blocked` with blocker kind `test-gap` and this op stops; it never authors the missing tests itself. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Restructure inside the declared write ceiling in the smallest behavior-preserving steps - move, rename, extract, inline, delete dead code - updating every inspected caller in the same change so the tree stays consistent and the adopted code conventions hold. Public contracts, persisted shapes, wire protocols, error identities and observable side effects stay identical; when the requested restructure cannot hold them, stop at the boundary and report the gap instead of editing behavior.

Run the SAME regression check AFTER the change, verbatim, on the restructured tree and record it beside the before run; where the machines ran before, run the SAME starci code-patterns check AFTER the change on the same roots and record it beside the before report. Parity means the same commands, same scope, same counts and the same green results; a different command, a narrowed selection, a new test failure or a new architecture/pattern violation is not parity - it is failed with the diff between the two outputs. Nothing is re-worded or skipped to make the after run look like the before run.

Review the actual diff and verify no unrelated or behavior-changing edit slipped in - the mapping of moved symbols to destinations must account for the whole change. Commit only when authorized, read back the full SHA/diff and prove the tested tree corresponds to that commit; otherwise report uncommitted honestly. Report done exactly once with both regression runs bound; never report a refactor that kept only a before run or only an after run. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion.

requirement.en: Run the record-class validator `starci validate`; every cited ID/path exists or is explicitly proposed, required assertions are covered, input bindings are current, and an honest not-run/fail cannot earn done.

The same declared regression check ran verbatim before AND after the change, on the exact before tree and the exact after tree, with both exit codes, counts and outputs recorded; the after result matches the before result. Where the slice lives in a checked FE/BE repository, the same starci code-patterns check ran verbatim on both sides with its reports retained; a new architecture or pattern violation after the change is a failure. A missing, different or narrowed check on either side is a failure, and no coverage at all is the `test-gap` blocker, never a silent pass.

The diff is explainable as pure restructuring - every changed symbol maps to a move, rename, extraction or equivalent rewrite, no public contract, persisted shape, error identity or observable side effect changed, and no feature or fix rode inside the change.
Inspect exact staged diff and actual tests; bind full real source commit(s), per repository, and separately retain integration/tested mappings. Report uncommitted or no-change honestly.

condition.en: No existing regression check covers the slice's observable behavior or the covering check cannot run in this environment. Report blocked with blocker kind `test-gap`; the graph routes it to test.author and this op never writes the missing coverage itself.
The requested restructure needs a path outside the selected write ceiling; report the exact paths as blocker kind shared-change rather than widening the allowlist.
The behavior to preserve is not settled by the accepted requirement - report blocked with blocker kind srs-gap, never pick a reading in code.
The design record is silent about the boundary or contract the restructure must hold - report blocked with blocker kind sds-gap, never invent the contract.

The declared regression runner, a declared architecture/code-pattern machine, a dependency or the sandbox cannot start here and the cause is provably unfixable from the allowlist - report blocked with blocker kind environment naming the exact missing piece.
Completing the request needs an authority the goal does not grant - report blocked with blocker kind authority, an owner decision, never a silent widening.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

Before owner presentation, srs.options contains at least two distinct concrete mutually exclusive policy outcomes in the exact presentation order. Questions beginning with Whether are agenda topics, not yes/no decisions. Repair an unprepared options array in this operation before requesting an answer.

action.en: Try the decided records first. When one settles the question, report done with the first line of the summary exactly "answered-from: <record id>" followed by the answer in one paragraph, and write nothing.

Otherwise write the one policy-decision record draft with the question, why it matters, the numbered options analysed per side, the decided records each touches by id in the text (never as a graph edge) and one recommendation. A provision is not prepared here; that is provision.ask.

Print the question and its numbered options in this terminal and say that the owner may answer here with the number, or later with workflow-answer; do not wait - a decision is taken provisionally on the recommendation and the owner overturns it later.

Run `starci validate` and report done exactly once: first line "decision: <record id>", then "recommended: <n>", then the options numbered as the owner will answer them. If the owner happened to answer here already, the first line is "answered-by-owner: <n>" instead.

requirement.en: A question a decided record settles is answered from that record, by id, and no record is written.

The question and its numbered options were printed in this operation's own terminal, with both ways to answer them, before any report was sent.

No value of any credential or secret appears in the record, the report, the terminal or anywhere else; a credential is put into the tree's encrypted identity custody by the owner's own command and this operation verifies only that it is present.

content.en: Keep the original assertion IDs and map each one to its scenario, the request it sends, the expected observable effect and the observed response. Record the exact commands, cwd, tested tree/commit, container services with their observed identity, exit codes, counts and sanitized output, including every attempt when a scenario was retried. Operator-specific observed result in E/result.md - report per assertion pass, fail with the observed response, or not-run with the reason.
