action.en: Freeze the assertion set before any effect and restate every assertion as a client request plus the observable effect the stack must show - status and error identity, response body, authorization denial and the persisted or emitted consequence. One assertion is one scenario; no assertion is merged, dropped or re-worded, and no expectation is inferred from how the code currently behaves. Where the requirement or the design is silent about the observable effect, record the gap and report it rather than guessing. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Inspect the existing suite and the declared stack before writing anything - how the suite starts its container services for the run, how it isolates and disposes them, which fixtures and helpers already exist, the naming convention of its specs, and the exact listed check commands with the manifest scripts behind them. Record that start path and the container identities. If the suite has no way to bring the real stack up itself, that is the reported blocker, not a reason to point the scenarios at a shared service.

Write or extend one scenario per assertion at the allowlisted spec paths, exercising the slice only through its public API - the transport contract a client actually calls - against the real stack the suite starts. Cover the positive path, the declared denial, invalid input and the applicable concurrency or replay case, and read the persisted effect back through that same public surface where one exists. Seed only the preconditions the scenario needs, through the suite's own fixtures, and never pre-create the outcome under proof. No mock, stub, fake or spy of the unit under proof and no in-process call that bypasses its entry point. Product code and declared expectations stay unchanged here.

Run exactly the listed check commands, verbatim, with the suite starting the real stack in this run; add no command, narrow no selection and skip no scenario. Keep the command, cwd, tested tree/commit, container identities, exit code, counts and sanitized output, and record every attempt when something was retried. Prove the stack actually served the scenarios - a scenario that stays green with its dependencies absent is a defect of the spec, and deleting or skipping a scenario is never a route to a green run.

Read the observed responses back against the frozen expectations, assertion by assertion, and keep every red scenario with the request it sent and the response it got. Then confirm the suite disposed the run-owned containers, volumes and scenario data it created, that no shared or production target was touched, and that no authorized external effect is left open. A leftover ephemeral resource is recorded with its exact identity and a resumable disposal command; unresolved effects cannot be presented as a clean run.

Report done exactly once, and only with a green run - every assertion covered by a scenario that ran on the real stack, the verbatim check commands with their exit codes, the run output and the spec paths, bound to the exact tested tree. A red scenario is failed, naming the assertion and the observed response; a stack that cannot start is failed with the exact reason; blocked with reason environment only when the cause is provably unfixable from the allowlist. Never report done on an unrun, skipped or partial spec, and never claim a proof from an earlier run. Validate bound evidence, keep the repair of any defect found here as a separate operation, and stop; never self-advance. For workflow execution submit the exact response to the coordinator gate, and when selected in a job matrix produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion.

requirement.en: `starci validate` ran; every cited ID and path exists or is explicitly proposed, the input bindings are current, and an honest not-run or fail cannot earn done.

Every required assertion maps to exactly one scenario that ran, with its original ID, its client request and its expected observable effect recorded before execution. A merged, re-worded, skipped or absent scenario leaves its assertion not-run.

Every scenario drives the slice only through its public API - the transport contract a client calls - with no mock, stub, fake or spy of the unit under proof and no in-process shortcut around its entry point. A user interface is not a proof surface for this op, and an image is never a response assertion.

The dependencies the slice needs ran for real in this run, brought up by the suite itself as run-owned containers with observed identities, and the scenarios were served by them. A green result with the stack absent is a spec defect, and a shared or production target is not an accepted substitute.

Exactly the listed check commands ran verbatim, with recorded exit codes, counts and retained sanitized output and every retry visible. A claimed pass without its output is not a run, and a stack that did not start is failed with the exact reason.

Only allowlisted scenario spec paths changed, proven by the actual repository status against the tested tree. No product file, schema or declared expectation was touched, and any defect found is reported as a finding for a separate repair.

The run-owned containers, volumes and scenario data are disposed and verified absent, no shared state was mutated, and any remaining ephemeral resource is recorded with its identity and a resumable disposal command.

content.en: Write only state/blocker/completion on this operation's own node; the revision belongs to the goal files and the diff to the evidence result.

Write goal v(n+1) whole - goal.json carries schema starci/workflow-goal@1, goal.md its human rendering - the only _local/workflows/<workflow>/ files this op writes; the kernel's run state (checks/, contracts/, inbox/, reports/) is never op output - rev bumped by exactly one, derivedFrom naming the previous rev and its digest, done still a checkable metrics block. Every changed section is carried at its new value; sections the revision did not touch are carried byte-identical. A direct edit that leaves no diff, a rev jump other than +1, or a done block the kernel cannot evaluate is not a revision.

Record the explicit diff - per section: unchanged, changed with old and new value, added, removed - the reason for each change, the derivations each changed section affects, and the authority classification of every edit. Operator-specific observed result in E/result.md: the rev transition, the section-level diff summary and the invalidation surface the kernel applies.

action.en: Bind the frozen goal, its rev and the requested change. Classify every requested edit before applying anything: content inside the approved envelope versus a scope, authority, allocation or done-metric change. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

A requested change that widens authority - new scope, new permitted effects, a relaxed metric, a new allocation the approval did not grant - is not applied. Report blocked with blocker kind authority naming the exact widening, or report ask with the typed options and one recommendation; the goal is never silently widened by an edit.

Apply the in-envelope edits and write goal v(n+1) - rev+1, derivedFrom the previous rev and digest, the explicit section diff recorded, the done block still checkable. Name every derivation each changed section affects so the kernel's invalidation machinery marks them stale; derivations themselves are never edited here.

Validate the new goal - `starci validate` over the node and evidence layout, goal.json carrying schema starci/workflow-goal@1, ids stable, done metrics still evaluable, rev exactly +1, diff complete - and report done once with the rev transition and the invalidation surface. Reports settled on the old rev stay bound to it and never count toward the new one.

requirement.en: The new goal bumps rev by exactly one, names its predecessor and digest, and the recorded diff accounts for every changed, added and removed section - a goal that differs without a diff, or a diff that does not match the files, is a failure not a revision.

No edit widened scope, permitted effects, allocation or relaxed a done metric; every such change was classified and escalated to an owner decision instead of applied. The new goal's authority is a subset of the approved one unless the owner answered otherwise.
The revised goal still carries a done block of checkable metrics and stable ids - a goal the kernel cannot evaluate is not a valid v(n+1) and is reported blocked, not written.
Every derivation a changed section affects is named for invalidation, and no derivation, report or evidence settled on rev n was rewritten or counted toward rev n+1.

condition.en: The requested revision would leave the goal without a checkable done block, with unstable ids or with an inconsistent rev chain; report the exact violation instead of writing it.

The revision changes scope, permitted effects, allocation or relaxes a done metric - report blocked with blocker kind authority naming the widening, or ask with typed options; never apply it silently.
The frozen goal or the requested change cannot be resolved - no approved goal to revise, or the change is not stated enough to diff; report the exact missing input.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

whenNot: Not for unapproved goals; not to widen scope/authority/allocation/done-metric - that is blocked authority or an owner ask.
Never rewrites derivations - it only names the sections each derivation depends on so the kernel can invalidate them.

goal.en: Grow the installed design grammar by one semantic unit the product needs and no composition of existing contracts renders, publish it from the grammar's own repository and record it in the canon.

scoped local commits when authorized
one published package version of the grammar when every gate of that repository is green
stories and tests executed in the grammar repository's declared sandbox

reads.path: selected grammar-gap report + the accepted requirement/design and interface design record it names

purpose.en: Read the reported gap exactly as it was raised - the shape the requester could not render, the screen, state and region it belongs to, and the accepted requirement and design that oblige it. The gap is the whole authority for what is grown; a unit nobody asked for is outside this job, and a gap that turns out to be a missing business rule or a missing screen is reported back rather than answered with a new component.

Read the WHOLE installed canon before deciding anything - every grammar family file (DNA, family, idioms, playbook), every frontend pattern and every UI composition, presentation and proof rule - plus the brand record the product is drawn inside. This is what determines whether the shape is already expressible: the existing contracts, their slots, their anatomy and the token, typography, spacing and icon vocabulary a new unit must reuse rather than extend.

Resolve the bound grammar repository, its actual checkout, root, HEAD and dirty state, and read its own conventions - how a contract component is declared, how slots and states are typed, where stories and tests live, which gates the repository runs and how it is versioned and published. The grammar is a separate repository with its own rules; this operation follows them instead of importing another repository's habits.

Read the consuming frontend repository's declared dependency on the grammar package - the exact package name and the version it currently resolves - so the published version can actually be bound after it exists. Reading the consumer is for the version binding and the import surface only; product screens are not this operation's to change.

reads.path: model/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Resolve this operator's request-bound external-agent chain from the selected StarCi skill and active profiles, and confirm the actual host can run the grammar repository's gates and reach its package registry before anything is published. Historical model names are not availability proof, and a host that cannot run a gate reports that limitation instead of publishing an unproven version.

content.en: Read the existing selected scope, expected assertions and .starciwork graph unchanged. Write only state/blocker/completion here; the unit, its anatomy, the composition attempt, the published version and the canon entries belong to the evidence result, not to semantic node prose. Missing refs/dependencies/acceptance require a reported gap or separately selected scope update; never add/remove them to obtain pass.

fields: grammar package source for the one new unit
the canon files the allowlist names

content.en: Write only the exact owned paths the allowlist names: the one new semantic unit in the grammar package with its stories and tests, the version bump that publishes it, and the canon entry that names it for every later drawing. Nothing else moves - no product page, no unrelated contract, no widened token set - and a destination outside the allowlist is a reported scope blocker rather than a wider write. The consumer's version binding is either inside this allowlist or a reported shared change; it is never edited silently.

writes.path: E/manifest.yaml + E/composition-attempt.md + E/unit.json + E/gates.json + E/publish.json + E/result.md

content.en: Retain the composition attempt in full - which existing contracts and blueprint regions were tried and exactly why the shape does not compose - because that is what makes a new unit justified rather than convenient. Then the unit itself (primitive or block, its anatomy, slots, states and the tokens it reuses), the stories and tests with the command, exit code and counts that show them red before and green after, every gate of the grammar repository with its real output, the exact published version with the registry read-back that proves it is visible, and the canon entries that now name the unit. Operator-specific observed result in E/result.md: the gap, the attempt, the unit, the version and the consumer binding. An unpublished version, an unread registry or an unrecorded canon entry is blocked or not-run, never pass.

action.en: Freeze the work before touching the grammar: restate the reported gap, the requirement and design that oblige it and the screen, state and region it belongs to, then read the whole canon and the brand and enumerate the existing contracts, slots and tokens that could carry it. Confirm the bound grammar repository is resolvable and clean and that the host can run its gates and reach its registry. A gap that is really a missing business rule or a missing screen is reported back to the record that owns it instead of being answered here.

Try the composition FIRST and write the attempt down: express the shape as existing contracts inside existing blueprint regions, naming each contract, each slot and each constraint. If it composes, the grammar is not short a word - report that composition as the answer and change nothing in the grammar, because the requester will draw it that way. Only a shape that demonstrably does not compose continues, and an ambiguity about whether it is really new is a question with the attempt attached, never a guess.

Name the one new semantic unit and implement it inside the allowlist, following the grammar repository's own conventions. A primitive is a fixed semantic unit and a block carries feature meaning; declare its anatomy, its named slots, every state it can be in and the tokens, typography, spacing and icons it reuses - none invented. Write its stories and its tests first and show them failing on the revision you started from; one unit per operation, never a family of them.

Run every gate the grammar repository declares, verbatim and on the same revision, and retain each command, exit code, counts and sanitized output. Only after every gate is green, publish one new version of the package and read it back from the registry until it is actually served - a registry may serve a new version minutes after it is accepted, and an unread version is not a published one. The publish is irreversible, so a red or unavailable gate is blocked or failed, never a publish.

Bind the published version in the consuming repository when that repository is inside the allowlist, and report it as a shared change with the exact paths when it is not; never edit a consumer silently and never leave the version unbound. Then record the unit in the canon - the grammar family files and the frontend pattern it belongs to - so a later drawing finds the word instead of asking for it again. Report once with the unit, the exact version, the canon entries and the consumer binding; no product page changed.

requirement.en: The attempt to express the shape as a composition of existing contracts and blueprint regions is recorded in full, names the contracts and slots it tried, and says exactly why it fails. A new unit without that record is unjustified, and a shape that composes cannot earn a grammar change at all.

Exactly one semantic unit was added, classified as a primitive (a fixed semantic unit) or a block (it carries feature meaning), with its anatomy, slots, states and reused tokens declared. A second unit, a widened token set or an invented colour, font or icon is a defect, not a larger delivery.

The unit's stories and tests exist at the repository's own locations, were red on the revision this operation started from and are green after it, with command, exit code and counts retained. A test that was already green proves nothing about the new unit.

Every gate the grammar repository declares passed on the published revision, and the published version was read back from the registry and found served. An inferred publish, a skipped gate or a version nobody could resolve cannot certify this operation.

The consuming repository resolves the published version - bound inside the allowlist or raised as a shared change with exact paths - and the canon names the new unit in the grammar family files and the frontend pattern it belongs to. No product page or screen changed.

condition.en: The reported shape is expressible as a composition of existing contracts and blueprint regions, so the grammar is not short a word. Report the composition and change nothing; the drawing or build that raised the gap renders it that way.

Whether the shape is genuinely a new semantic unit, or which of primitive and block it is, cannot be settled from the canon, the gap and the accepted records. Report the question with the composition attempt attached; never guess an identity into the grammar.

A gate the grammar repository declares cannot run, fails, or the package registry cannot be reached or does not serve the version after publication. Report it; a published version without green gates and a registry read-back is never a delivered unit.

A required change - a consumer manifest, a second repository, a canon file the allowlist omits - lies outside the paths this operation may write. Report the exact paths and wait; never widen the write ceiling and never touch a product page to close the gap.

The grammar repository, the canon, the brand record or the accepted requirement this operation depends on is missing or not effectively done. Report node/resource IDs; never author the missing record or run a predecessor here.

operators.goal: Prove one declared external integration against the real provider, in its sandbox account, with the credential the owner supplies, read at the moment of use from the tree's own encrypted identity custody, and keep the live exchange as evidence.

goal.en: Prove one declared external integration against the real provider, in its sandbox account, with the credential the owner supplies, read at the moment of use from the tree's own encrypted identity custody, and keep the live exchange as evidence.

sideEffects: one live exchange with the declared provider's sandbox account, inside the scenario's declared scope
scenario-owned data created in that sandbox account and disposed by the same run

reading the owner-provided credential through sops from the declared identity custody (.starciwork/_resources/identity/<slug>/secrets.enc.yaml), inside the checking process only, never writing its value

graphPolicy.location: .starciwork node dependsOn/refs with direct sourceRefs and collocated assets

purpose.en: When the selected scope touches application deployment, .starcistacks, bootstrap or recovery, load the whole-application dev/VPS contract. Reconcile component ownership, encrypted credential custody, lifecycle commands and existing consumers. Run `starci stacks check` when validating a materialized stack; bind its exact inputs and limitations. Acceptance additionally requires the selected real startup, persistence, recovery and application checks. This conditional read grants no extra deployment or source scope.

reads.path: current provider official documentation + owning integration declaration preparation

purpose.en: Read the official sources before deciding authentication, account, scopes, lifecycle, configuration or owner prerequisites. Keep actual read dates and supported observations in the owning preparation; callbacks and webhooks are assessed for this intended use, never assumed universal. Missing research returns to the owning operation before credential input. Research completeness, executable setup, owner input and successful live verification are distinct states.

Read the existing selected integration node: which declared integration it proves, its assertions, its declared refs and dependencies and its validator freshness. This consumer op requires its target node to exist. An absent target is a scope/graph gap; report it and propose a separately selected scope op. Never create the node, never invent its assertions, and never re-word one so a scenario that already ran can be called a pass.

Read the declaration the business or architecture record made: the integration id, the provider, the sandbox account to use, and the credential entry - its exact variable name, that the owner provides it, and the custody identity:<slug> that holds it. This declaration, not the source, says which provider is under proof and which variable carries the key. A declaration that names no credential variable, or no custody, is a reported gap, never a guessed name and never a key read from somewhere else.

Read the declared contract with the external system - the request the product sends, the response and error identities it expects, the retry, idempotency and timeout boundaries, and what the product must do when the provider refuses. These define, per assertion, the exchange the scenario performs and the effect the provider must show. Where the design is silent about the observable effect, report the gap instead of inventing an expectation.

Resolve the repository resource, actual checkout/root/HEAD and dirty state, and read the delivered client of this integration - its entry point, its configuration and the variable it actually reads the credential from. The proof binds the exact tested tree, so a claim without a resolved repository and a named client is not a proof.

reads.path: .starciwork/_resources/identity/<slug>/secrets.enc.yaml, read with sops at the moment of use

purpose.en: Resolve the owner-provided credential by the exact variable name the declaration gives, out of the custody the declaration names, and nothing else: run the check inside `sops exec-env <that file> '<check>'` so the value exists only in that one process. It is never invented, never defaulted, never read from a second variable that looks similar, never exported into a shell or an .env file and never taken from a checked-in file. No sops, no key for this tree, no such custody or no such variable in it is reported `blocked` with reason `environment` naming the slug and that exact variable, which is the owner's question; it is never a reason to fake the provider, skip the assertion or report a pass. The value authenticates the live call and is written nowhere - not into a record, a report, a log or a chat.

reads.path: current request authorization + declared sandbox account allowed effects

purpose.en: Bind the live exchange and the scenario-owned data it creates to the selected assertions and to the sandbox account the declaration names. A production account, a real customer's channel or an unbounded retry is outside this op; discover an unknown external outcome by read-only correlation before repeating an attempt.

reads.path: model/registry.json + selected runtime execution profile + actual host tools/model

purpose.en: Resolve this operator's request-bound external-agent chain from the selected StarCi skill and active profiles, and the actual host network and tool availability the live call needs. Capabilities are the intersection of actual tools, selected profile policy, op permissions and existing task authority.

reads.path: selected workflow request + workflows/contracts.json + this op authority.json

purpose.en: When selected inside the named workflow, read the exact request, strict response contract and primary/secondary authority JSON. Standalone op execution does not invent a workflow request.

content.en: Read the existing selected scope, expected assertions and .starciwork graph unchanged. Write only state/blocker/completion here; the exchange itself, the observed responses and the findings belong to the evidence result. Missing refs/dependencies/assertions require a reported gap or a separately selected scope update; never add or remove them to obtain pass.

writes.path: E/manifest.yaml + E/scenario.yaml + E/exchange.json + E/run-output.txt + E/readback.json + E/result.md

content.en: Keep the original assertion IDs and map each one to the exchange it performed: the request the product sent to the provider, the expected observable effect, and the response the provider actually returned, read back through the provider's own surface where one exists. Record the provider, the sandbox account identity as observed rather than as configured, the credential variable name with no value, the exact commands, cwd, tested tree/commit, exit codes and sanitized output, including every attempt when something was retried. The manifest carries `proof: {boundary: live, fakes: []}`; a run that stood in for the provider is not this proof and is recorded as a spec defect. Every credential, token, personal identifier and provider secret is redacted before the assets are hashed.

Only for the selected named workflow, emit the response defined by workflows/contracts.json. Return outputs.results for every input assertion with the provider it reached, the observed response identity and the run output reference. A failed or blocked response preserves evidence with outputs null, and a blocked one names the exact missing credential variable.

action.en: Validate the declaration's documentation-backed preparation before any credential request or live effect. Read the primary sources and check each interpretation independently; a URL alone is not research evidence. Complete authorized machine-owned setup before asking for owner-only actions; setup that depends on those actions follows them in the recorded order. Report inaccessible docs as a research failure and a missing preparation as an owning-record gap, never as a missing secret.

Freeze the assertion set before any effect and restate every assertion as one exchange with the declared provider plus the observable effect it must show - the accepted response and its identity, the declared refusal, the invalid-input case and the applicable retry or idempotency case. One assertion is one exchange; no assertion is merged, dropped or re-worded, and no expectation is inferred from how the client currently behaves. Record the provider, the sandbox account and the exact credential variable name the declaration gives.

Run everything that needs the credential inside `sops exec-env .starciwork/_resources/identity/<slug>/secrets.enc.yaml '<command>'`, so the value is resolved from exactly that variable in exactly that process and nowhere else. If sops is not installed, the key for this tree is unavailable, or that custody holds no such variable, stop here and report `blocked` with reason `environment` naming the slug and the variable, so the owner can provide it: do not substitute a second variable, do not export it into the shell or an .env file, do not read a key out of the repository, do not generate one, and do not continue with the provider replaced by a stand-in. Confirm the resolved account is the declared sandbox one by observing the provider's own answer rather than by trusting a hostname, and confirm the effects this run is authorized to cause.

Write the scenario beside its evidence and drive it through the delivered client - the same entry point the product uses, reading the same variable - so what is proven is the product's own path to the provider; where the product runs from a materialized .starcistacks deployment, reach it through the declared components, never an improvised address. No mock, stub, fake, spy, recorded cassette or in-process shortcut may stand in for the declared provider anywhere in this scenario; a stand-in is the defect this operation exists to catch, not a fallback when the provider is awkward. Create only the preconditions the exchange needs, inside the sandbox account.

Run the scenario against the live provider and keep what happened - the request as sent with every secret redacted, the response as received with its status and error identity, timings, exit codes and every attempt when something was retried. Then read the effect back through the provider's own surface where one exists, so a send that the provider accepted but never delivered is visible. A scenario that stays green with the credential removed is a defect of the scenario, not a pass.

Dispose the scenario-owned data this run created in the sandbox account and confirm it is gone, and confirm no authorized external effect is left open. A leftover remote resource is recorded with its exact identity and a resumable disposal command; unresolved effects cannot be presented as a clean run. Nothing that could carry the credential value leaves this step.

Report done exactly once, and only with a live green run - every assertion covered by an exchange that actually reached the declared provider, with the manifest's `proof.boundary` set to `live` and `proof.fakes` empty, bound to the exact tested tree. A refused or wrong response is failed, naming the assertion and what the provider returned; a missing credential is blocked with reason `environment` and the exact variable name; an unreachable provider is blocked with reason `environment` and the observed failure. Never report done on an unrun, skipped or faked exchange, and never claim a proof from an earlier run. Keep the repair of any defect found here as a separate operation, and stop; never self-advance. For workflow execution submit the exact response to the coordinator gate. If the declared live check explicitly identifies an invalid or expired credential, report blocked/environment with --credential-request-file naming a JSON file containing exactly reason (invalid or expired), variables (the declared names), and check (the declared failing check name). Keep its nonzero exit and safe observed evidence in checks. Include no value, custody path or baseline: the kernel binds replacement to the tested custody version and owns the input form. Generic provider errors, scope/configuration defects and outages do not authorize credential replacement.

requirement.en: `starci validate` ran; every cited ID and path exists or is explicitly proposed, the input bindings are current, and an honest not-run or fail cannot earn done.

The integration under proof is the one a business or architecture record declared, with its provider, its sandbox account and its credential variable named in that declaration. An integration the tree does not declare is not proven here and is reported as a gap.

Every assertion was proven by an exchange that reached the declared provider itself, through the delivered client, with no mock, stub, fake, spy or recorded response standing in for it anywhere in the scenario. The manifest records proof.boundary live with no fakes, and a stand-in makes the run a spec defect rather than a proof.

The credential came from the exact variable the declaration names, out of the identity custody it names, read through sops at the moment of use and from nowhere else; it was never invented, defaulted, substituted, exported into a shell or an .env file, or silently skipped, and its value appears in no record, report, asset, log or message. A custody that cannot give it is blocked with the slug and that variable named.

The observed effect was read back through the provider's own surface where one exists, so an accepted request that produced no effect is visible. Every attempt is retained with its request redacted and its response as received.

The scenario-owned data created in the sandbox account is disposed and verified absent, no production or shared account was touched, and any remaining remote resource is recorded with its identity and a resumable disposal command.

condition.en: No business or architecture record declares this integration, or its declaration names no provider, no sandbox account, no credential variable or no credential custody, so what to call and what to authenticate with cannot be stated. Report the gap; never infer the provider, the variable or the custody from source.

The declared identity custody holds no value under the exact variable the declaration names. After official research and executable setup, report blocked with reason environment, the slug and that variable name so the kernel presents its workflow-owned form in Orca or hidden fill prompt on a headless host. Missing sops or a host decryption key is a setup failure: repair it within authority or report its actual environment/authority boundary, never ask for another provider credential to fix it. Never invent, default, substitute or skip a key, fall back to an environment variable, or replace the provider with a stand-in to proceed.

The declared provider's sandbox cannot be reached in this environment - no network egress, a refused host, an unavailable endpoint or an exhausted quota - and the cause is provably unfixable from the allowlist.

The delivered client of this integration does not exist, exposes no entry point a scenario can drive, or reads its credential from somewhere the declaration does not name; report the finding instead of writing a second client beside it.
Proving an assertion would require changing product code, configuration or a declared expectation outside the allowlisted paths; report the finding and never widen the ceiling.

A declared prerequisite is not effectively done, or a required declared input/scope is missing. Report node/resource IDs and propose a separately selected graph update when needed; never run predecessors or weaken dependsOn/refs/required to proceed.

The record governs. A slot the record does not declare is not generated here, and a record that declares no slot at all leaves this operation nothing to do; neither is a licence to decide what the screen should contain.

Open the actual chosen candidate image beside the record and the crop each slot names inside it, so the artwork that is produced is the artwork that was approved rather than a fresh interpretation of its brief. A slot whose crop cannot be located in the candidate is a reported gap, never a free redraw.

Read the product brand record the kernel attaches - its colour tokens, its mascot and logo masters with the placements each one allows and forbids, and its imagery prompt rules - and read the actual master files a slot references. These rules bound every prompt and every result; a brief that cannot be honoured inside them is reported, not quietly widened, and an asset is never produced from a master the record forbids in that placement.

Resolve the bound repository, its checkout and its owned asset paths, and read whatever already exists at the slot's destination, so an existing verified asset is reused or replaced deliberately instead of duplicated under a second name. Reading the surrounding code is for placing the file only; this operation changes no product code.

content.en: Write each slot's artwork at the owned asset path the allowlist names, in the declared format and at the declared pixel size, one file per slot and nothing else. No source file, no stylesheet, no component and no configuration is edited here: wiring the file into a component is the build's step, and an asset written outside the allowlisted asset paths is a reported scope blocker rather than a wider write.

Record the produced artwork on the work/node@2 record against the slots it already declares: per slot the repository path of the file, its sha256, its status and the tool provenance of the generation, and bind each path in the record's asset list so the bytes are covered. Add no slot, remove no slot and rewrite no brief, region, size or crop: those are the drawing's, and a slot that turned out wrong is a reported gap, not an edit of what was approved. A slot with no file is left explicitly unproduced with its reason.

Retain the slot-to-file table as readable YAML, the full prompt and reference list used per slot (including the candidate crop and each brand master passed as a reference), the real tool provenance, and the inspection of every produced file against its brief and the brand rules. Record an honest unproduced or failed slot; a slot reported as produced without opened bytes is a failure, not a draft.

action.en: Read the declared artwork slots of the design record and freeze the work before generating anything: per slot its id, screen, state, blueprint region, purpose, brief, pixel size and viewport, format, brand references and the crop of the chosen candidate it came from. Open the candidate and locate every crop. Confirm the host actually carries an image generator. Compare each brief against the brand rules and the placements its referenced masters allow, and settle which slots are producible before the first image is requested; an embedded artwork visible in the candidate that the record never declared is reported rather than invented into a slot here.

Generate each producible slot with the image model, passing the candidate crop and the brand mascot or logo masters the slot references as actual input references, so the result is the approved artwork rather than a new one matching the same words. Produce exactly the declared pixel size and format, one file per slot, at the owned asset path the allowlist names, reusing a verified existing file instead of writing a second copy of the same artwork under another name. Do not drift the brief, do not restyle the candidate, do not add or remove content the region does not carry, and do not touch product code.

Open every produced file and inspect it as bytes and as an image against its slot - the crop it must reproduce, its declared size and format, and the brand rules and placement its references allow. Then record each slot's file path, sha256, status and provenance back into the design record and bind the path in its asset list. A file that differs from the approved crop, misses its declared size or breaks a brand rule is regenerated or reported; it is never recorded as the slot's asset.

Report once with the complete slot-to-file table, naming every declared slot and the file that now carries it. A slot whose brief cannot be honoured inside the brand rules is blocked as a brand gap with the exact rule and the exact brief that conflict. Artwork the candidate embeds that the record never declared is blocked as an interface gap naming the screen, state and region, so the drawing declares it instead of this operation guessing at it. An asset path outside the allowlist is blocked with the exact paths. Stop without wiring anything into a component and without advancing the workflow.

requirement.en: Every artwork slot the design record declares is accounted for - produced with a file and sha256, or explicitly unproduced with a named blocker. A partial table reported as complete, or a slot silently dropped, is a failure.

Each produced file was opened and compared against the candidate crop its slot names, at the declared pixel size and format. A generated image that reinterprets the approved artwork instead of reproducing it does not satisfy its slot, and a similar-looking result is not proof of the same artwork.

Every prompt and every result stayed inside the brand record: the referenced masters were passed as real references, the placement each master allows was respected, and no colour, mark or imagery rule the record forbids was produced. A visual acceptance does not substitute for the record's own rules.

Every recorded path exists in the bound repository with the recorded sha256, every path is inside the allowlisted asset scope, the declared slot briefs, regions, sizes and crops are byte-identical to what the drawing authored, and no product code changed. An honest not-run cannot earn done.

condition.en: A slot's brief cannot be honoured inside the brand record - the placement its master requires is forbidden, the imagery rules contradict the brief, or the record names no master the brief depends on - so any asset produced would be outside the brand. Report the rule and the brief; never widen the rules.

The chosen candidate embeds artwork the design record does not declare as a slot, or a declared slot names a crop, region or state the candidate and the record do not contain, so the brief would have to be authored here. Report the screen, state and region for the drawing to declare.
The resolved profile and actual host carry no image generator, so no slot can be produced. Report the limitation; a scripted, hand-drawn or placeholder file is never a generated asset.
A slot's destination lies outside the owned asset paths this operation may write. Report the exact paths and wait; never widen the write ceiling to place a file.

The design record, the chosen candidate or the brand record this operation depends on is missing or not effectively done. Report the node/resource IDs; never author the missing record, draw the missing candidate or run a predecessor here.

Keep every required screen and reachable state, then add `ui.coverage`: scale, representativeScreens and a map of screen/state/viewport to actual Grammar components, derivation and optional directionAsset. Enumerate every required screen, reachable state and responsive band from accepted journeys/SDS; map each combination to actual inspected Grammar components and state contracts. Classify the scope as bounded or large. For a large task choose the smallest representative set of critical screens that covers the highest-risk layouts, interactions, brand moments and component anatomy; do not generate one image for every state. A missing product decision, SDS behavior or Grammar capability is a typed blocker, never filled with visual invention.

Build one exact prompt per representative direction from accepted business/SDS, brand rules/masters, relevant UI knowledge and actual Grammar anatomy/reference inputs. Include real product-shaped content, screen purpose, component regions, state, viewport, accessibility and forbidden treatments. Invoke built-in `image_gen.imagegen`; a browser capture, hand-painted boxes, mockup export or prose-only substitute does not satisfy this operation. Save the returned image and exact prompt, open the image, review it, and record the actual tool provenance. Do not claim an image-model name the tool did not expose.

Declare every embedded illustration/mascot/decorative/media region as an artworkSlots entry for `interface.asset`. Update the complete coverage map so every non-generated screen/state says which representative direction it derives from, which actual Grammar components implement it and how its state differs.

Validate Work and every artifact hash, then report the representative images, prompt artifacts, actual tool provenance and complete coverage map. State the truth boundary: the generated direction is a design input, not exact component/render/API evidence. `interface.implement` must produce actual Grammar implementation captures and code checks; `uat.verify` must independently exercise the running product in a browser. Resolve shared layouts, responsive variants, sequential states and ambiguous alternatives explicitly. For repairs reproduce the original defect and preserve its evidence. Own preparation through delivery: inspect readiness and reproduce the requested defect when applicable, partition the selected work into cohesive changes and check callers before editing. Resolve repository-local dependencies and bounded development runtime needs under the existing scope. Shared library changes belong to the actual FE or BE package owner: include owner tests, packaging/export compatibility and selected consumer integration proof in this same implementation; never publish a package implicitly. The frontend worker waits and never edits SDS. Orca runs architecture.decide in a separate child worktree; after coordinator review/integration, start a fresh frontend attempt from that SDS revision and rerun affected implementation, render and quality checks. A business/SRS, owner or accepted-scope change is blocked for the user instead.

Map every relevant region across all draws to routes, shared/owned components, API reads/actions, states, ACs and actual knowledge rules/cases. Business governs behavior; images express accepted visual intent within applicable knowledge and installed component constraints. Record missing screens/states and cross-image or knowledge conflicts; do not average incompatible alternatives, invent behavior from pictures or weaken the selected graph.

Implement the mapped screens and shared layout once using actual installed components, tokens and repository conventions. Apply scoped creation, refinement or the smallest defect repair; retain cross-image consistency, responsive behavior, keyboard and focus. Follow applicable knowledge even where literal image copying would violate it; unresolved material design conflicts remain blocked. Account for every asset visible in every input draw. Reuse a verified matching asset or create/generate the required asset, inspect it and integrate its actual source file. Claude with no image-generation capability may reserve a blank decorative slot with a deferred brief; never use invented URLs, broken images or label pending art complete. Implement applicable loading, empty, error, denied, success and recovery states from the accepted business/API contracts, including required states not depicted in draws. Never guess endpoints, fake success or invent undisclosed business decisions. CALL POINT (step 4): if an observed API integration or render-data defect blocks an already accepted journey and is repairable without business changes, read interface.implement/secondary.json and call its listed backend.implement role. Pass the exact backend repository, allowed file paths, defect evidence/problem, changeKind and unchanged businessRefs. Set FE to waiting in this same cell. If no such defect exists, skip this call. If the repair needs business/schema/authorization changes or an unlisted operator, return blocked with the missing decision. Resume this step only after every required support response matches its request and passes every required criterion in the caller-owned secondary.json, including scope, business preservation, API compatibility, implementation quality and commit verification; inspect returned changes, integrate the actual commits and continue to step 5. Defects discovered in steps 5 or 6 return to this call point under the same permissions; never create an implicit helper.

Run relevant component/unit, interaction, type, lint and build checks for mapped ACs/states and applicable knowledge. For repairs retain before/after evidence for the original unchanged expected assertion plus collateral regressions. Fix only within scope; keep failed or untested required behavior visible. This implement op owns lint, typecheck, relevant tests/coverage, affected builds and Sonar. Resolve real repository scripts and CI thresholds; record command, source tree/commit, result and sanitized logs. Cut mode. Turn the cut node into a derived parent: remove its state, its completion and its write scope and keep its assertions as the group's acceptance under extensions.work3.groupAssertions, because a parent with children authors no state and derives one from them. Then run the record-class validator `starci validate` over the edited tree and confirm the parent is derived and every child is launchable on its own. Record the seam, the children and the write scope of each. Build nothing and change no product source; the kernel launches the seam first, fans the rest out behind it and proves the whole group once.

requirement.en: The node declares a non-empty write scope and at least one check, every authored assertion is named by a check that proves it, and the workspace validator passes over the edited tree. An honest not-run or failing validator cannot earn done.

Every path in the write scope was inspected in the actual source and is consistent with the referenced design; every check command exists in the repository and was run or explicitly reported as unrunnable. A fabricated path or command is a failure, not a draft.

In record mode the node's description, refs, dependsOn, required flag and state are byte-identical to what was authored. In cut mode the node keeps its description and refs and loses exactly its state, its completion and its write scope, which is what makes it a derived parent. In both modes no completion or kernel extension block was written, nothing under the evidence folder of the record was edited, and no node outside the cut node's own folder changed.

Cut mode: exactly one child is named the seam, every other child names it in dependsOn, and no two children share a path - each write scope is at most twelve inspected files and is disjoint from every sibling and from the seam. Every child is one observable behaviour with one runnable check per assertion and every assertion traced to the same requirement and design ids the parent traced to, and the parent keeps its assertions as extensions.work3.groupAssertions with no state, completion or write scope of its own. A node reported as cut: none left the tree byte-identical. Overlapping children are a failure, not a draft: two operations that write the same file are one merge conflict with two authors, never parallel work.
